question.worked_solution:
First, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} & =d-\frac{5}{7} \\ d-\frac{5}{7} & =-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To isolate $d$, we need to perform the *opposite* of subtracting $\frac{5}{7}$ from $d$, which is *adding* $\frac{5}{7}$ to $d.$ Remember to perform the same operation on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}d-\frac{5}{7} & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ d-\frac{5}{7}+(\frac{5}{7}) & =-\frac{3}{2}+(\frac{5}{7}) \\ d+0 & =-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{5}{7} \\ d & =\frac{-3\cdot 7+5\cdot 2}{14} \\ d & =-\frac{11}{14}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
